claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my daughter Alex. She's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently living with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask about her education or training status.

Is Alex currently in full-time education (such as A-levels, or equivalent), or enrolled on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not in any education or training at the moment. She left school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in full-time education or approved training, I have one more important question:

Has Alex recently turned 16, and if so, when was her 16th birthday? Also, has she registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar government training or employment service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She turned 16 a few months ago. No, she hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more question to confirm:

What is Alex's date of birth? Specifically, I need to know whether her birthday falls before or after 1st September, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility when a child leaves education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Her birthday is in March, so it was before September.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful.

Just to clarify the timing a bit more: when did Alex leave school? Was it at the end of the last academic year (around summer), or more recently?

The reason I ask is that Child Benefit normally continues until the 31st August after a child turns 16, or until the first of these dates if they leave education:
- The last day of February
- The last day of May
- The last day of August

This helps me understand if you're still within an eligible period or not.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She left school at the end of last summer, around the end of August when term finished.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining. Just one more clarification to help me assess this accurately:

When you say "last summer," do you mean August 2024 (this past summer) or August 2023 (the summer before)? This will help me determine if the Child Benefit eligibility period has ended or not.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I mean this past summer - August 2024.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 16 years old (turned 16 in March 2024, before 1st September)
- She left school at the end of August 2024
- She is not currently in full-time education or approved training
- She has not registered with a careers service or similar

Child Benefit typically continues until the 31st August after a child turns 16 if they leave full-time education. Since Alex turned 16 in March 2024 and left school at the end of August 2024, the Child Benefit eligibility would have ended on 31st August 2024.

For Child Benefit to continue beyond this point, Alex would need to either:
1. Be in full-time non-advanced education (e.g., A-levels, BTECs), or
2. Be on an approved training course, or
3. Be registered with a qualifying careers or training service (in some limited circumstances)

Since none of these currently apply to Alex, I'm now ready to provide my eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Alex turned 16 in March 2024 and left school at the end of August 2024. Child Benefit for a child who has left education continues until the 31st August after they turn 16. Since that date has now passed, and Alex is:
- Not in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels or equivalent)
- Not on an approved training course
- Not registered with a careers service

...the eligibility criteria are no longer met.

**What could change this:**

If Alex decides to return to full-time education (e.g., college, sixth form) or starts an approved training course before she turns 18, you may become eligible again. You would need to notify the Child Benefit Office if her circumstances change.

I hope this information is helpful. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.

Child Benefit eligibility for a child who leaves education continues until the 31st August after they turn 16. Since Alex turned 16 before September and left school at the end of August 2024, the eligibility period ended on 31st August 2024. For Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16, the child must remain in full-time non-advanced education, be on an approved training course, or in certain circumstances be registered with a careers service. Alex is not in education or training and has not registered with a careers service, therefore she no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
